classification.difficultyReason: Use segment addition and the supplied product relation to form a quadratic, apply the formula and reject the negative length.

content.prompt:
The interval $AB$ is extended to point $P$ so that $AB\times AP=BP^2$.

If $AB=8\text{ cm}$, find the lengths of $AP$ and $BP$.

spec.sourceRegion: Exercise 5F question 6, between the condition and final instruction
spec.description: A horizontal segment with marked points A, B and P in that order, with labels below. Ordinary source blue lines and red point markers use house black.
spec.mathematics: A, B and P are collinear; B lies strictly between A and P. No numerical lengths appear in the figure.
spec.answerVisibility: All three points and labels are permanent givens; no answers are shown.

inlines.text: Use AP = AB + BP to form a quadratic, then retain the positive length.

answer.worked:
Let $BP=x\text{ cm}$, where $x>0$. Then $AP=(x+8)\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}8(x+8)&=x^2\\8x+64&=x^2\\x^2-8x-64&=0\end{align*}$$
Here $a=1$, $b=-8$ and $c=-64$.
$$\begin{align*}b^2-4ac&=(-8)^2-4(1)(-64)\\b^2-4ac&=320\\x&=\frac{8\pm\sqrt{320}}{2}\\x&=4\pm4\sqrt5\end{align*}$$
Reject $4-4\sqrt5$ because it is negative. Therefore,
$$\begin{align*}BP&=(4+4\sqrt5)\text{ cm}\\AP&=8+(4+4\sqrt5)\text{ cm}\\AP&=(12+4\sqrt5)\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
Check: $8(12+4\sqrt5)=96+32\sqrt5$ and $(4+4\sqrt5)^2=96+32\sqrt5$, so $AB\times AP=BP^2$.
